title: Blind and low-vision participants complete everyday tasks with Be My AI in peer-reviewed interview studies
summary: Peer-reviewed interview studies record blind users completing everyday tasks with Be My AI, e.g., airport gate numbers, a handwritten check.
account: Xie and colleagues at Pennsylvania State University interviewed 14 visually impaired users of Be My AI, the large-multimodal-model image-description feature of the Be My Eyes app, and analyzed image descriptions gathered from 25 September 2023 to 31 March 2024; the paper appeared at CHI 2025. Individual uses are recorded: 'P2 utilized it to identify gate numbers at the airport', 'P10 used it to recognize her surroundings when disoriented in her neighborhood', and P13 received a description locating 'a hair tie in the upper right hand corner' of a carpet. A separate ASSETS 2025 interview study of 21 participants (November 2024 to January 2025) records P9 using Be My AI to read a handwritten check. The date observed is Be My AI's public release date, 25 September 2023, which is the start of the first paper's social-media collection window; the interview participants' uses are undated. Outcomes are self-reported.
purpose: Be My AI was built to describe photographed scenes and objects to blind and low-vision users; these task completions were that purpose. Xie et al. state that Be My AI is built on OpenAI's GPT-4 models.
system: Be My AI (large-multimodal-model image description in the Be My Eyes app)
developer: Be My Eyes (feature built on OpenAI's GPT-4)
deployer: Be My Eyes (consumer app used by study participants)
taxonomy_note: Both studies also document hallucinations and errors; the record covers only the attributed task uses quoted.

ratings.reason: Everyday tasks (gate numbers, orientation, locating a dropped item, reading a check) completed independently by identifiable participants; small, self-reported, and the same papers document frequent errors.

ai_role.statement: The multimodal model generated the descriptions participants acted on; no independent per-task accuracy check was made, and participants themselves reported risk (P9: 'I knew there was a risk').

paired_incident.title: Error-Prone AI Accessibility Tools Reportedly Lead to Navigation Issues for Blind Internet Users
paired_incident.basis: Same stakeholders and task: AI describing visual content for blind users; Be My AI read gate numbers and a cheque, while AI accessibility overlays mislabelled web content, misleading blind and visually impaired people such as Jakob Rosin.

headline: Be My AI reads airport gate numbers and a check for blind users

revisions.change: Record drafted from the cited sources.
Paired with AI Incident Database incident 830 (medium confidence); severity not given by the source.

Added the GPT-4 basis that Xie et al. state (the record had said no source names the model vendor), removed P1's pregnancy-test reading from the echo because the source reports inconsistent results rather than a completed task, explained that the observation date is Be My AI's release date and that the interview uses are undated, and matched the arXiv v1 title's unhyphenated 'Low Vision'.

claim_basis: One independent peer-reviewed study, one independent preprint and one other independent source are on file. There is no finding by a regulator or court.
